observations.behavior: Adds documentation and metadata for a new MCP tool 'external-data-destinations-add-sources' which attaches warehouse sources to a destination, including checks for destination status and resync behavior.
observations.code_quote: "description": "Attach up to 50 existing sources to a destination. Each source's tables then also sync there, except tables with their own destination override: they keep the override and ignore this link. Before attaching, check the destination's status with external-data-destinations-retrieve: do not attach to a failing or paused destination until the user fixed it. Then call external-data-sources-destinations-retrieve for each source. When destination_ids holds only the PostHog warehouse destination (is_posthog_warehouse in external-data-destinations-list), the source may write there by default and would stop updating its PostHog tables after this call. If the user wants to keep them and no destination in external-data-destinations-list is paused, first call external-data-sources-destinations-update with that same list: it makes the warehouse an explicit link. If a destination is paused, tell the user instead. When destination_ids is empty, tell the user the PostHog tables stop updating. Call external-data-schemas-destinations-retrieve for each of the source's tables and tell the user which have inherits_from_source false: those will not reach this destination. Sources already attached, or already at the destination limit, come back in skipped with a reason. An attached source sends only rows from its next syncs, so the destination holds no history until those tables are resynced. Set resync=true to start a full resync of every enabled table now, including tables with an override that will not reach this destination. Tell the user first: a resync re-reads every row and bills every destination the source writes to.",
observations.posthog_connection: Defines the expected behavior and API contract for attaching warehouse sources, including dependency on warehouse-multi-destination feature flag and specific API operations.

observations.behavior: Adds documentation and metadata for a new MCP tool 'external-data-destinations-connect-link' which generates a secure browser link for warehouse destination setup.
observations.code_quote: "description": "First step to add a warehouse destination (Postgres, Redshift, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, S3 or Azure Blob). Returns a browser link where the user enters the credentials in PostHog, plus the next steps in `instructions`. For S3-compatible storage (MinIO, Wasabi, R2, GCS), pass integration_kind='s3-compatible'. Never ask the user to paste passwords, keys or tokens into the chat.",
observations.posthog_connection: Establishes the secure credential handling flow for warehouse destination setup, gated by warehouse-multi-destination feature flag.

observations.behavior: Adds documentation and metadata for a new MCP tool 'external-data-destinations-create' which creates a warehouse destination, including connection testing and configuration parameters.
observations.code_quote: "description": "Create a place where warehouse sources write synced rows, from an integration that holds the credentials. Get the integration id with external-data-destinations-connect-link first. Pass type, a name, the integration id and the target config for the type: Postgres and Redshift take database and schema; Snowflake takes database, schema, warehouse and optional role; BigQuery takes dataset and optional project; Databricks takes http_path, catalog, schema and volume; S3 takes bucket, region and optional prefix and compression; Azure Blob takes container_name and optional prefix and compression. Every type except Redshift tests the connection on create, and a failed test returns a 400 that names the field to fix. Redshift has no test, so a wrong target only shows up when the first sync fails. The target cannot change after creation, so confirm it with the user first. A new destination receives nothing until a source is attached with external-data-destinations-add-sources.",
observations.posthog_connection: Defines the warehouse destination creation and connection testing behavior, including Redshift exception and dependency on warehouse-multi-destination feature flag.
